title: Joining King Oliver's Plantation band: personnel, shows and saxophone chair
summary: Howard left Dave Payton's band for Oliver's Dixie Syncopators at the Plantation, names the ten players, and describes his arranging and playing first alto.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Well, I'll let you ask the questions. Alright. Go ahead. How did you happen to join Oliver's band?
Oh. That's right. I joined Oliver's band before I went to Shanghai.
That's right. I'm telling you you're jumping all over. Well, I can't remember all of them. You just ask me the question. I'll tell you. I'll ask you the questions.
How did you do that? I'm telling you you're jumping all over.

Well, I can't remember all of them. You just ask me the question. I'll tell you. I'll ask you the questions. I was working with Dave Payton band out to the Persian Palace. That's a Persian hotel at 64th and Cottage. Al Turner had the place. Used to have the Grand Auto Inn where later it was the plantation in Chicago. And I got a nice offer to go down and play with them and I left this band and went, left Dave Payton and went to the plantation with Joe. And I left the band. Who was? That was in 1924. That's after I came back from Europe.
In whose band? All of them. Bonnie Bigard, Albert Nicholas, Bud Scott, Bob Schockner, Trumpet.

King Oliver, George Feely, Paul Barberin, Bert Cobb on bass. That's all I think. Ten of us. What kind of a band was it? We were playing shows and then playing Dixie Lamb music. They called them the Dixie Lamb music. They called them the Dixie Syncopators. We saw those.
Were there arrangers for that band?
Yes. Special or stock? I had specials and stock. And stock.
Did you ever do any arranging? Yes.
Sure did. Where did that band play?

At the Plantation in Chicago. Why Smith were you playing with them? I played on three of them, but I mean sax and playing it. What kind of sax? Altum. E flat altum. Third altum. No, they had me playing first on that. Two times I like to die when I went in the band. When Buster left Fletcher Henderson. Buster Bailey? Yeah. Well I knew that he was on the third, you know. And I just know he's a first saxophone player. When they put me in the band, the first thing they do is pass out these books and I get the first book. I pass it on, you know. I said, no, no, you keep that. I'm like, oh. You know, first saxophone, that's a responsibility, you know. Sure. That's what he had me on. Joe Oliver, too. Oh yeah?
Whose playing was the Clanness of those? Me and Nick, Albert Nicholas. Albert Nicholas. Both of us. Barney didn't play Clanness, only in the arrangements then.
Tenor? Yeah. He took all the tenor courses.
